spec.title: codkit PROP-015: The delivery of the Codkit runtime into the own layer of a product

status.comment: the universal delivery mechanism: the managed copy, runtime load|check, the delivered files in verify/save/inventory, the generator contract. What the library contains, and what the generators write, are the project type's answers and moved to modules/vscode/PROP-007 and PROP-008 in the PROP-016 split of 2026-09-09, leaving tombstones here; decisions of 2026-09-07

purpose.title: 1. Purpose and the form of delivery

p.RT-PURPOSE: Tombstone (PROP-016 split, 2026-09-09): moved to spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-007#RT-PURPOSE; the address stays for citations.

facts.RT-IS-A-MANAGED-COPY: The library is delivered into a product as a **managed copy**, like the standards package: `codkit runtime load` copies the version directory from toolRoot into `<patchesDir>/delta/own/codkit/`, and a plain `codkit load` carries it on into `<tree>/src/vs/<ownDirName>/codkit/`; the copy is compared with the shipped version byte for byte; an edit in place is drift; an update arrives only with a new version of Codkit (`RT-LOAD-UPGRADE`). What the library **contains** is the project type's answer and lives in the type's module (VS Code type: `spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-007#root`); this document keeps the delivery mechanism alone.
facts.RT-DIRECTORY-IS-CODKIT: The directory of the library in the own layer is called `codkit/` (not `kit/`, not `lib/`): the name states the owner of the code unambiguously and matches the prefix of the licence scope (PROP-014 §4a `STD-NOTICE-SCOPE-BY-PATHS`). The internal identifiers of the library (service decorators, the ids of contributions, of commands and of storage keys) live in the `codkit` namespace; the identifiers of the features, the settings and the context keys of a product carry the prefix of the product and are set by its declarations.
facts.RT-SHIPPED-LOCATION: A runtime library is a **package of a project type**: in toolRoot it lives in `runtime/<packageId>/v<semver>/`, exactly one version directory under the named package (as in `STD-PACKAGE-LOCATION`), and the installation may carry one such package per type that has a library at all. Which package is delivered is the type's answer and never a guess from the directory listing (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-RUNTIME`); the `vscode` type names `runtime-vscode`. A `packageId` the installation does not carry is `CK-E-RUNTIME-PACKAGE` naming the identifier and the expected directory — a damaged installation, or a type built against another codkit — and a type with no `runtime` area refuses earlier still, with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY` (`RT-LOAD-STEPS` step 0). The `runtime/` directory is listed in the `files` of `package.json` and travels in the tarball. The content of the version directory is exactly the tree that lands in `delta/own/codkit/` (without the notice file, which belongs to PROP-014 §4a).
facts.RT-VERSION-LITERAL: The version of the library is the directory name `v<semver>` and the literal `export const CODKIT_RUNTIME_VERSION = '<semver>';` in `common/version.ts`; a divergence is `CK-E-RUNTIME-PACKAGE`. The same file holds `CODKIT_RUNTIME_VERIFIED_UPSTREAM: readonly string[]`, the upstream tags on which the library has been compiled and verified. The number is **1.0.0**, the development version every package this tool ships carries (`DEV-VERSION-IS-1-0-0` in the conventions, owner ruling of 2026-09-08): the library is changed in place under it, a product takes the changed copy with `codkit runtime load --upgrade`, and the directory `v0.1.1` it lived in before the ruling moved to `v1.0.0` with no change of content.
facts.RT-ONLY-TS-AND-MD: Tombstone (PROP-016 split, 2026-09-09): moved to spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-007#RT-ONLY-TS-AND-MD; the address stays for citations.
facts.RT-EVERY-FILE-CARRIES-THE-BANNER: Every file of the library carries a licence carrier per PROP-014 §2: the four notice lines (the copyright, the English and the Russian links to UPL, `SPDX-License-Identifier: UPL-1.0`) in the comment style of its own extension (`//` for `.ts`, `<!-- -->` for `.md`) in the first lines of the file. The shipped directory passes `LIC-CHECK-ALGORITHM` with zero problems: this is checked by `shippedRuntime.test.ts` in `npm run floor` and by the licence gate of `runtime load` before any write.
facts.RT-NO-PRODUCT-NAMES: The library carries the name of no product; the examples in the comments and in the tests use neutral identifiers (`acme.sample`).

facts.RT-SHIPPED-RUNTIME-TEST: `packages/codkit/test/unit/shippedRuntime.test.ts` in `npm run floor`: exactly one version directory; the version literal equals the name of the directory; only `.ts`/`.md`; the four header lines in every file; `checkLicenseCarriers` → 0 problems; the imports per `RT-NARROW-UPSTREAM-SURFACE`; no product names; no non-ASCII outside the comments of the header.

commands.title: 4. The `runtime load|check` commands; delivered files in `verify`, `save`, `inventory`

facts.RT-LOAD-STEPS: `codkit runtime load [--dry-run] [--upgrade]` (patchesDir and `codkit.json`, the tree is not read): (0) the project type declares `runtime-library`, otherwise `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`, exit 2, and it names the runtime package to deliver; (1) the source is the single version directory under `runtime/<packageId>/` in toolRoot and the version literal (`RT-VERSION-LITERAL`; otherwise `CK-E-RUNTIME-PACKAGE`, exit 2); (2) the licence gate is `LIC-CHECK-ALGORITHM` over the version directory with the policy of Codkit → 0 problems, otherwise `CK-E-LICENSE-PACKAGE` with the list, exit 2 and not a single write; (3) the target `delta/own/codkit/` without the notice file: `absent` / `identical` / `drift` by a comparison of the trees; a `drift` without `--upgrade` is `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` with the paths, exit 1 and not a single write; (4) `--dry-run` prints the plan (the created/replaced/removed paths) and exits 0; (5) the directory is written into a temporary directory and renamed as a whole, and the notice file in the target is preserved; (6) the notice goes into both roots per PROP-014 §4a (`STD-LOAD-STEP-WRITE-NOTICE`, the block of components); (7) the report `{ command: 'runtime load', version, target, state: 'created' | 'upgraded' | 'unchanged', files: { written, removed }, notice }` and three hints: the graft `import '../codkit/browser/featureFlags.contribution.js';` in the composition root of the product, the `code-import-patterns` block per `LAYERS.md`, and the first feature through `codkit gen feature`.
facts.RT-LOAD-UPGRADE: `--upgrade` replaces the directory as a whole without comparing it with the previous version (Codkit keeps no old versions and does not merge): it prints the list of the removed and the replaced paths; without the flag any drift is a refusal, so edits to what was delivered are lost only by an explicit decision.
facts.RT-CHECK: `codkit runtime check` is read-only: `identical` → 0; `absent` → 0 with the text `runtime not installed`; `drift` → `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` with the paths, exit 1; plus the state of the copies of the notice per PROP-014 §4a. `--json`: `data: {target:{state, version, paths}, noticeFiles}` - the same key as `standards check` has (PROP-007 §25 `CMD-RUNTIME-CHECK`).
facts.RT-DELIVERED-NOT-OWN: The files under `delta/own/codkit/**` are delivered by Codkit (PROP-005 `OWN-DELIVERED-BY-CODKIT`): they are not covered by units and do not count as code of the product; `verify` compares the installed copy with the shipped version (`CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` on a difference) and rejects an own unit with a root inside `codkit/` (`CK-E-OWN-UNDER-CODKIT`).
facts.RT-SAVE-REFUSES-DELIVERED-EDITS: `save` refuses with `CK-E-DELIVERED-EDIT` and a list when a file of the tree under `src/vs/<ownDirName>/codkit/**` differs from `delta/own/codkit/**` or is absent from the delta; nothing is mirrored. Hint: change it in Codkit and run `runtime load --upgrade`.
facts.RT-INVENTORY-ENTRY: The inventory shows the installed library as one synthetic entry `CK-codkit-runtime` (layer `own`, category `delivered`, a `reason` carrying the version), not as files.
facts.RT-PUBLISH-KEEPS-THE-RUNTIME: The release branch of `publish` carries the files of the library: each of them carries its own header, and the condition of UPL is satisfied; only the notice file is excluded (PROP-014 §4a `STD-NOTICE-RELEASE-EXCLUSION`).

facts.GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS: The generated files are code of the product: the header is written from `--holder`/`--license` (the year is `--year` or the current one) in one of two styles. `--header-style line` (the default) is four `//` lines: the copyright first, then `Licensed under the <title>.`, then `The full text is <licence file> of this repository.`, the SPDX line last; without a title the licence identifier stands in its place, without a file name the words `the licence file`. `--header-style block` is a block comment of the upstream shape: the line `/*---…---`, ` * Copyright (c) <year> <holder>`, ` * All rights reserved. Licensed under the <title>; the full text is <licence file> of this repository.`, ` * SPDX-License-Identifier: <license>`, the line ` *---…---*/` - so that the own code of a product looks like the upstream code next to it (`MI-SAME-SHAPE-AS-UPSTREAMS-PARALLEL-SYSTEM`). In both styles the copyright line carries the year and the holder and nothing after them, so the carrier parser of PROP-014 reads the holder exactly (decision of 2026-11-01: the earlier block form put `. All rights reserved.` on the same line, and the consumer check of PROP-019 read a foreign holder; a unit test now runs both styles through that check). `--header-file <path>` (a path relative to patchesDir) writes the header verbatim from a file of the product - for shapes that the fields cannot express; the file must end with a line break; it does not combine with `--holder`/`--license`/`--year`/`--header-style` - exit 2, nothing written. `--header-style` without `--holder`/`--license` is exit 2 (there is nothing to shape). Without the header flags the files are written with no header and with the warning `no header written; pass --holder and --license, or --header-file`. When the patch set carries `codkit.licensing.json`, the fields come from the selected profile instead and the flags must agree with it (PROP-019 `HEADER-FROM-PROFILE`); `no header written` cannot happen while a profile is selected. The header of Codkit is never written into the files of a product.

facts.GEN-REFUSES-EXISTING: If at least one target file exists - `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS` with the path, exit 1, nothing written.

facts.RT-COMPAT-DECLARATION: `CODKIT_RUNTIME_VERIFIED_UPSTREAM` lists the upstream tags on which the current version of the library has been compiled by the harness and has passed its tests; `runtime load` prints a warning when the pin of the product (`codkit.json` `pin.tag`) is not in the list.
facts.RT-SEMVER: The API of the library towards the features of a product (`registerFeature`, `IFeatureFlagsService`, `IFeatureDescriptor`, `createBrandTransform`) is versioned semantically; a breaking change is a new major version, and `runtime load --upgrade` across a major prints a warning with the list of changes from the `README.md` of the library.
facts.RT-CYCLE-GATE: The upgrade cycle (`codkit cycle`) on a new pin first of all compiles the installed library and runs its tests in the fork tree; a red result names the file of the adapter and the assumption. The rule is written down; the implementation is the next campaign.

p.DECISION-RT-MANAGED-COPY:
**Decision:** the library is delivered as a managed copy under the control of Codkit rather than generated once.
**Why:** three products with three diverged editions of the flags service is exactly what the owner wanted to avoid; the mechanism of delivered own files already exists (`LICENSE-CODKIT.md`).
**Considered and rejected:** - "generate and forget" (`flags gen` literally) - the fixes never reach the products; - a vibe package - it does not deliver TypeScript into `src/`; - writing the service in every product - duplication and divergence.
**When to revisit:** if products start editing the delivered files more often than once per cycle - then part of the library moves into generated skeletons.

p.DECISION-RT-NAME-CODKIT:
**Decision:** the directory `codkit/`, and the identifiers of the library in the `codkit` namespace.
**Why:** `kit` is a common word and may collide with a directory of the product; `codkit` names the owner and matches the prefix of the licence scope.
**Considered and rejected:** `kit/`, `lib/`, `vendor/`.
**When to revisit:** not planned.

p.DECISION-RT-UPGRADE-FLAG:
**Decision:** a version update is `--upgrade`, which replaces the directory as a whole; without the flag any drift is a refusal.
**Why:** Codkit keeps no past versions, so "an edit of the product" cannot be told from "an old version"; the explicit flag makes the loss of edits deliberate.
**Considered and rejected:** a three-way merge - there is no base; an automatic replacement - it loses edits silently.
**When to revisit:** if Codkit starts keeping a manifest of the hashes of past versions.
